title: SKU hyperthreading & I/O path deltas: A100/H100/L40S throughput-latency mapping
content:
Purpose:
This doc records an exploratory benchmark focused on the interaction between host CPU hyperthreading/irq affinity and the device I/O path (NVLink vs PCIe) across three representative GPU families: A100, H100, and L40S. Goal is to surface practical knobs that materially change tail latency for small-batch inference and sustained throughput for long-context workloads.

Why this is different:
- Existing benches look at driver/cuda and raw kernel breakdowns; this one intentionally ties host scheduling (HT, CPU isolation, IRQ pinning, NUMA bind) to observed GPU-side stalls and host->device memcpy deltas.
- We capture short microbursts (50–500 requests/sec) and steady-state large-sequence throughput to show regime-dependent behavior.

Environments tested (cloud SKUs):
- AWS p5.48xlarge (H100, NVLink) with NVIDIA driver 545.46 + CUDA 12.2
- AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100, NVLink) with NVIDIA driver 535.113 + CUDA 12.1
- GCP a2-highgpu-8g (A100, PCIe) with driver 535.104 + CUDA 12.1
- GCP l40s-standard-16 (L40S, PCIe) with driver 545.20 + CUDA 12.2
Note: we chose both NVLink-enabled and PCIe-only instances to separate inter-GPU fabric effects from host I/O scheduling.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- CPU modes: HT on (default), HT off (BIOS), and HT logical-cpu-isolation (Linux isolcpus + irqbalance off)
- IRQ affinity: default vs explicit pin to isolated CPUs (no user-space interference)
- NUMA binding: process pinned to local NUMA node vs remote
- CUDA streams/concurrency: single-stream decode vs multi-stream batching (N streams)
- Batch sizes: small (1–4 tokens per request, typical chat turns), medium (64 tokens), large (1024 tokens)
- Workload types: short-prefill+decode (chat), long-prefill (context-heavy), KV-warm cache hit/miss toggles

Tools & traces captured:
- nvprof/Nsight compute high level kernel timings (where available), nsys for end-to-end traces
- perf top/record on host during steady-state and burst windows
- iostat/mpstat for host IO/CPU metrics and nvml-based GPU utilization + memory copy counters
- strace sample to validate syscall patterns during bursts
- small in-house tracer that captures request enter/exit times and per-token latency for each worker (attached as artifact)

Key findings (summary):
1) Hyperthreading off often reduces p99 for small-batch chat-style workloads on A100 NVLink setups, but shows negligible or slightly negative effect on H100 NVLink runs.
   - A100 (p4d): HT off -> p99 down by ~18–24% for single-stream small-batch; p50 unchanged.
   - H100 (p5): HT off -> p99 changes within ±5%, but throughput at high concurrency sometimes decreased (3–7%).
   Interpretation: On A100 NVLink configurations we saw host-side scheduling jitter (syscalls and memcpy bursts) that collided with the GPU kernel launch window; disabling HT reduces logical CPU contention and improves host-to-device ramp. H100's microarchitecture and driver maturity seem to be more resilient to that jitter.

2) IRQ pinning to isolated CPUs gives consistent wins for tail latency on PCIe L40S instances where DMA interrupts are more frequent and share CPU with user-space threads.
   - L40S (GCP): IRQ pinned -> p99 improved 20–30% in small-batch tests; mean CPU steal/interrupt time dropped substantially.

3) NVLink multi-GPU prefill paths mask some host scheduling issues: when prefill is split across GPUs via NVLink the host-to-device memcpy becomes less of a serial bottleneck.
   - NVLink machines show 10–15% higher sustained tokens/sec for long-context workloads when using multi-GPU prefill, while PCIe variants plateau earlier.

4) Driver version deltas matter for memcpy path: driver 545 showed better async memcpy overlap with compute on H100 vs 535 on A100 in our workload shapes. But this is workload dependent; for small token decodes the difference is minor.

Representative numbers (single-worker, single-GPU, chat-style small-batch):

| SKU   | CPU mode | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | p99 (ms) | tokens/sec |
|-------|----------|----------|----------|----------|------------|
| A100 NVLink (p4d) | HT on  | 12       | 52       | 118      | 980        |
| A100 NVLink (p4d) | HT off | 11       | 42       | 92       | 975        |
| H100 NVLink (p5)  | HT on  | 9        | 38       | 72       | 1040       |
| H100 NVLink (p5)  | HT off | 9        | 36       | 70       | 1000       |
| L40S PCIe (gcp)   | default| 14       | 68       | 160      | 820        |
| L40S PCIe (gcp)   | irq pinned| 13    | 48       | 112      | 900        |

Observability signals we used to correlate behavior:
- perf showed increased context-switch and softirq time correlated with p99 spikes on p4d.
- nsys timelines show host memcpy bursts clustered before a batch decode leading to kernel queueing on A100 with HT on.
- nvml memory copy counters confirmed higher sync copies on PCIe L40S in default configuration (no IRQ pinning).

Detailed notes / anomalies:
- On one H100 run (driver 545.46), we observed a kernel launch stall that self-resolved after ~40s; captured nsys snapshot shows repeated tiny kernel restarts. Logged to ENG-2121.
- GCP A100 PCIe instance had significantly higher PCIe write latencies under host CPU load vs GCP's NVLink-enabled SKU. This suggests platform-level PCIe topology/config matters more than raw GPU family.
- NUMA misbind (process on remote node) caused catastrophic throughput drops (40–60%) across all SKUs; always ensure process pinned to local NUMA with GPUs.

Practical recommendations (short-term):
- For A100 NVLink clusters used for low-latency chat, experiment with HT off on instance types where we control BIOS or use CPU isolation to reduce jitter. Add to Dedicated instance provisioning checklist.
- For PCIe-heavy fleets (L40S), enforce IRQ affinity + isolate CPUs for inference worker threads. Consider a sysctl/udev rule template.
- Add driver 545.x to our compatibility smoke matrix for H100-heavy customers; flag kernel-launch stall patterns in rollout playbook.
- Update our prefill orchestration to prefer NVLink-aware prefill when multi-GPU available and context length > 512 tokens. This is a routing policy candidate for Optimize.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Repeat these runs with our steady-state multi-tenant mix (5 tenants, mixed batch sizes) to see interference effects.
- Run microbench that pins interrupts to one core and exercises more aggressive GPU kernel concurrency to measure when HT helps.
- Automated nightly regression against driver versions 535.x and 545.x for representative workloads; capture nsys + perf artifacts for any p99 drift >10%.

Artifacts attached / where to find traces:
- nsight/ directory (nsys traces named by sku-date-config)
- perf/recordings (flamegraphs)
- scripts/run-cpu-configs.sh (isolation+irq pin helper)
- traces.zip (per-request latencies and metadata)

Questions for reviewers:
- Should we make HT-off a recommended option in Dedicated onboarding for certain SKUs? (ops cost vs perf tradeoff)
- Any objections to adding IRQ affinity enforcement as a default systemd unit for our L40S PCIe node images?

Author notes (quick):
- Repro scripts live in the linked PR. Results vary by cloud region and instance firmware; use the attached traces as canonical evidence for further investigation.
